chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the adhan, and he said:

"Recite it aloud and raise your voice with it. Then when you perform the iqamah, let it be lower than that. And do not wait with your adhan and your iqamah except for the entering of the time of salat, and recite your iqamah swiftly."

key_terms.أَقَمْتَ: you performed the iqamah, the second call before salat
key_terms.إِقَامَتَكَ: your iqamah, the call commencing the prayer
key_terms.الْأَذَانِ: the call announcing the time of salat
key_terms.حَدْرًا: swiftly and in a flowing manner
key_terms.صَوْتَكَ: your voice, meaning vocal volume in recitation
key_terms.وَقْتِ الصَّلَاةِ: the time when salat has entered

ai.seo_question: How should the adhan and iqamah be recited according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a practical ruling on how the adhan and iqamah should be delivered. The adhan is to be proclaimed loudly, while the iqamah is given in a lower voice, and both are tied to the entrance of the prayer time, with the iqamah being recited swiftly.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.876 - Muawiya ibn Wahb asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about the adhan (call to prayer).
The Imam said: "

Raise your voice and speak loudly when giving the adhan. When performing the iqamah (second call to prayer), use a slightly lower voice.
Do not delay your adhan and iqamah except until the time for prayer has arrived, and recite the iqamah quickly (with fluidity)."
